title: $Rp_*$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(-,\cO_E)$ is a left adjoint for proper $p$
statement:
Let $E\subseteq\Qlb$ be a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $\cO_E$, let
$\Lambda=\underline{\cO}_E$ ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]), and let $p\colon Z\to Y$ be a proper
morphism of the setting. Then the derived pushforward
$Rp_*\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Z,\underline{\cO}_E)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y,\underline{\cO}_E)$
of [def-sfb-dc-lower-star] has a right adjoint $Rp^!$.

external.place: On each level $\cO_E/\varpi^n$, the étale $Rp^!$ exists (SGA 4, XVIII) and preserves bounded constructible complexes (SGA 4½, *Th. finitude*).
On each level $\cO_E/\varpi^n$, the étale $Rp^!$ exists (SGA 4, XVIII) and preserves bounded constructible complexes (SGA 4½, *Th. finitude*).
The levels are compatible with reduction, and their derived limit is right adjoint to $Rp_*$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(-,\underline{\cO}_E)$ (Bhatt–Scholze, §6.8).
The levels are compatible with reduction, and their derived limit is right adjoint to $Rp_*$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(-,\underline{\cO}_E)$ (Bhatt–Scholze, §6.8).

proof.text: Put $\Lambda=\underline{\cO}_E$. Both $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(T,\Lambda)$ of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] and $\Dbc(T,\cO_E)$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible] are the full subcategory of the derived category of $\Lambda_T$-modules consisting of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology, for $T=Z,Y$. Thus these are the same categories with the same morphisms; no change to discrete constant coefficients is made. For integral coefficients [sk-lem-integral-models] gives $\Dctf(T,\cO_E)=\Dbc(T,\cO_E)$. Write $\mathcal C_T$ for this common category.

source.place: Opening equality Dctf=Dbc; definitions of Dcons and Dbc

proof.text: The coefficient $\cO_E$ is admissible in the explicit list of [sk-def-localizing-closure], since $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite. By the setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], $Z$ and $Y$ are separated finite-type schemes over the standing field $k$, of characteristic different from $\ell$, and $p$ is a morphism of these schemes. Apply [sk-thm-existence] (2)--(4) with $f=p$ and integral coefficients. On $\mathcal T_T=\Loc(\mathcal C_T)$ it supplies a functor $F=Rp_!$ and an exact right adjoint $G=p^!$, with $F(\mathcal C_Z)\subseteq\mathcal C_Y$ and $G(\mathcal C_Y)\subseteq\mathcal C_Z$. In particular both restrictions are functors; preservation by the right adjoint is part (4), not a consequence of Brown representability alone.

For proper $p$, clause (1) of [det-cor-existence-ii-restriction] gives a natural isomorphism $F\cong Rp_*|_{\mathcal T_Z}$. This is the proper compactification comparison: $Z\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}Z\xrightarrow{p}Y$ is an admissible compactification and its extension-by-zero factor is the identity. The cited clause supplies the comparison with the chosen compactification, so equality is not inferred merely by substituting a different choice into a definition. On $\mathcal C_Z$ the resulting restricted ambient pushforward is exactly the functor of [def-sfb-dc-lower-star].

source.place: Clause (1): proper lower shriek is restricted ambient direct image

proof.text:
Define $Rp^!:=G|_{\mathcal C_Y}$. For $K\in\mathcal C_Z$ and $L\in\mathcal C_Y$, the full inclusions from [sk-def-localizing-closure] and Step 1, the natural isomorphism in Step 3, and the adjunction in [sk-thm-existence] (3) give
$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_Y}(Rp_*K,L)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_Y}(Rp_*K,L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_Y}(FK,L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_Z}(K,GL)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_Z}(K,Rp^!L).
$$
Every bijection is natural in $K,L$: the middle ones come from a natural functor isomorphism and an adjunction, and the equalities are those of full subcategories. These bijections are precisely an adjunction for the stated $Rp_*$ and $Rp^!$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$.

source.place: Proof, part (2): natural Hom bijection along full inclusions

proof_origin.place: Opening proper identity-compactification argument, parts (3)--(4) of sk-thm-existence, and detailed restriction in sk-cor-existence-ii-restriction
